It's a little early so let me try and follow on this subject accurately. I don't really feel obligated to accept and reconcile the substandard content of series I enjoy rather I just accept as fact "this is what i'm going to get". I don't have the personal finances or ability to generate this kind of content myself, and must rely on the industry. **What has incessant complaining gotten any fan of a series?**(edit, case in point my last post is already -1 before finishing this one. Just talking about it leads to people hating on you for pointing out perfectly justifiable things). Mostly derision and a justification to why a story can be lacking. It's just a tired argument. I rather spend time justifying my enjoyment rather than justifying my dislike for a product, while still recognizing for certain intellectual properties that just can't happen. Mostly two major gaming franchises. The lack of attention to any details firmly established are things I can't reconcile.  Now for me *how* things work in a universe does matter to a good degree. To avoid spoilers in this thread I'll use one of those gaming franchises as an example. A corporation created the famous virus that created mutants in a location on the west coast that was a top secret research facility with 1 other location being the nearby military base shortly before the nuclear bombs fell that created the world of that game. In a later installment, it inexplicably shows up on the East Coast in a different corporation's facility. These 2 corporations had no relation, and were in fact competitors. I feel this is sloppy story telling. Back to the space opera, I felt it was a good movie. For me, 2 details could of been included to make it a much better movie without significantly changing any of the story. But that is a spoiler. Going back to addressing universe mechanics, it's actually why I really enjoyed a universe created by author Patrick Rothfuss. In his book magic works on a sort of voodoo level. A good example is if a character wanted to light a candle on the other side of the room, he needs heat. One option is to draw their own body heat to the level needed to light the wick, but that kind of drain can lead to cold shivers. There are quite a few options though. I really like a universe that has a reason why things work. Although personally I don't think the force ever needed midichlorians. Ever.

Recognizing these are works of fiction the closest parallel I can give is real history. You don't get to just alter it. On the flip side there's the comic book approach. No one story is sacred, and any number of different spins have been done. I appreciate both. A famous fantasy series is a series of the former. A famous superhero is a series of the latter.  I actually prefer the comic book approach as it doesn't taint whatever continuity has been established in a particular timeline. And the creatives are allowed to work with what they want in respect to those timelines, or any new ones.  Believe me the extremes of other side of the aisle are bad. The prequel episodes for example did pay decent respect to the history and timeline of most things, while lacking any execution. It was miserable. While the latest episode seems to have excellent execution with only a brief glaze of the actual space opera universe slapped on. So really there's 2 options. Go with the one universe timeline and pay respect (or don't) to the timeline, or go multiverse and take liberties with it as much as you please.  Funny thing is one of the gaming franchises is attempting to do the multiverse thing while still making it canon and it's just terrible.
